examples of clips used for truth telling.

parts.text: Explain why Loftus and Pickrell made this statement.

parts.label: (b)

text: In the study by Loftus and Pickrell (false memories), they state that they cannot make claims
about the percentage of people who might be misled by false suggestions.

What two types of study did Piliavin et al. suggest would be necessary to fully understand the

did not support diffusion of responsibility.

parts.text: Explain one advantage of using an experiment in this study rather than a case study.

text: The study by Bandura et al. (aggression) was an experiment. Alternatively, they could have
conducted a case study on a child.

parts.text: Describe what is meant by the ‘ego’.

parts.text: Explain the importance of Hans’s ego in his psychosexual development.

text: In the study about little Hans, Freud refers to the ‘ego’.

unattractive faces of babies.

parts.text:

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe how the children were tested on their moral understanding immediately after seeing
the drawings.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The children were then asked to point to one of several faces. Explain how this test was
different from the one you have just described.

text: In the study by Nelson, the children saw drawings of a story and were tested on their moral
understanding.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: What physical effects did the researchers intend the epinephrine injections to have?

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Explain why the researchers did not use the data from these five participants.

text: In the study by Schachter and Singer (emotion), some participants were given injections
of epinephrine (adrenaline). Five participants did not experience the intended effects of the
epinephrine, so their results were not used.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what researchers are able to learn about sleep from an EEG.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The EEG electrodes were gathered into a single cord at the top of the participant’s head.
Explain why this was done.

text: In the study by Dement and Kleitman (sleep and dreaming), an electroencephalograph (EEG) was
used.

parts.text: Identify one of these conditions and explain how the results differed from the control (baseline).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe why there was a difference between experimental results and those from the control
(baseline) task.

text: In the study by Maguire et al. (taxi drivers), speech output was recorded in four experimental
conditions.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe one way in which the study by Demattè et al. is more valid than the previous study.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Identify and explain one problem with the Demattè et al. study.

text: Prior to the study by Demattè et al. (smells and facial attractiveness), other researchers had shown
that smelling perfume could make pictures of people seem more attractive, when compared to the
smell of banana.

Section B (20 marks)
Answer both questions in this section.

text: The study by Billington et al. tested students using the SQ-R, which investigates systemising in
various domains. One example is the ‘spatial’ domain, which includes the system of map reading.
All systems share the same overall structure.
